Chapter 7: Completing the Unfinished Survival Responses.
You know, one of the core ideas in healing trauma is something called “completing the cycle.”
Imagine this—when your body reacts to a threat, whether it’s fighting, running away, or freezing up, that energy is supposed to help you survive. But if something interrupts you—if you never get to finish that response—some of that energy just gets stuck inside.
The real path to feeling better? It’s about letting your body finish what it started, even if the event happened ages ago.
Here’s the surprising part: it doesn’t have to be dramatic. Most of the time, it’s actually pretty subtle. You might notice little movements, a sudden urge to stretch, a shiver, or maybe the need to take a deep breath. That’s your nervous system trying to tie up loose ends.
So, what helps this process along?
First, it’s all about listening to your body. Whenever you’re in a safe moment, pay attention to those tiny impulses—maybe you want to move, sigh, or even just shift in your seat. Those urges are important.
Next, let yourself move in whatever natural way comes up. Trembling, sighing, or just adjusting your posture—these aren’t random. They’re your body’s way of letting go of stuck energy.
And most important? Stay present. When you’re grounded in the here and now, your body feels safe enough to finally let go.
Want a real-world example? Picture someone who’s been through a car accident. Maybe they never had a chance to run or even cry after it happened. Later, in a calm moment, they might feel like stomping their feet or shaking out their hands. By letting those movements happen, they’re actually allowing their body to finish what it started. The hold of trauma begins to loosen.
Remember, this doesn’t need to be forced—or turned into a big production. Healing is gentle, and the body knows what it needs. Over time, by completing these cycles, you can start to feel more in charge, more alive, and just... more yourself.
